promptLatex: A fair six-sided die is rolled twice. What is the probability that at least one of the two rolls shows a $6$?
hintLatex: The complementary event has no six on either roll, which makes both rolls come from five faces.
There are $6 \cdot 6 = 36$ ordered pairs, and $5 \cdot 5 = 25$ of them contain no six at all.
solutionLatex:
The sample space is the $36$ ordered pairs of faces.

The complementary event is that neither roll is a $6$. Each roll then has $5$ possibilities, so there are $5 \cdot 5 = 25$ such pairs.

Therefore $P(\text{at least one six}) = 1 - \frac{25}{36} = \frac{11}{36}$.
